articles.summary: Planet Labs PBC (NYSE: PL), a leading provider of daily data and insights about change on Earth, today released its first light image from Pelican-12, an updated second generation (Gen 2) high-resolution Pelican™ satellite, captured over Luanda, the capital city of Angola. The image was taken on October 30, 2026, from an altitude of approximately 589 km, following Pelican-12’s launch aboard SpaceX's Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. As the spacecraft completes its instrument calibration process and approaches its final operational orbit, image quality is expected to further improve. Luanda, Angola • October 30, 2026 • Altitude: 589 km • Pelican-12 Pelican-12 is Planet’s 25th satellite brought to orbit this year across four successful launches, showcasing the speed, innovation, and consistency of Planet’s agile aerospace approach. articles.summary: Planet Labs PBC (NYSE:PL), a leading provider of daily data and insights about change on Earth, today announced that it plans to release its fiscal third quarter 2027 financial results for the quarter that ended October 31, 2026, after market close on Thursday, December 10, 2026. Planet’s management will host a conference call to discuss the financial results and business outlook at 5:00 p.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. PT the same day. Planet invites you to listen to the conference call, which will be webcast live at Planet’s Investor Relations website ( investors.planet.com ). The webcast will be archived on this website and available for replay approximately two hours after the completion of the event. articles.summary: Planet Labs PBC (NYSE: PL), a leading provider of daily data and insights about change on Earth, today announced a multi-launch agreement with Stoke Space Technologies, Inc. , a developer of fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicles, to provide expanded launch capacity for Planet’s constellation fleet. Under the agreement, Planet receives primary payload rights, granting critical scheduling flexibility to specify launch dates and target orbital planes for its payloads. articles.title: Planet and Stoke Space Sign Multi-Launch Agreement for Nova Launch Capabilities
